clips.text: Your sweat is medicine. Not metaphorically — chemically. A 47-amino-acid protein called dermcidin, made by your own skin, kills germs on contact.
It wakes up in salt and acid — the exact chemistry of a workout — and punches holes in bacteria like E. coli and staph.
Your skin even hires allies: one resident bacterium makes its own antibiotic that hunts drug-resistant MRSA.
And twice a day, you wash the whole army away. Hot water, soap, scrubbing — the shower is a siege engine.
The good news: within ten minutes, the garrison starts moving back in. So here's the loop back to the start.
Your sweat is an antibiotic. Every drop carries a 47-amino-acid protein that punches holes in germs — and your body makes it without asking, every single day.
